newsitem.title: GERMANY: Growth chances in E.European stainless steel muted.
newsitem.headline: Growth chances in E.European stainless steel muted.

text.p: Opportunities in expanding the production and consumption of stainless steel in eastern Europe are limited by a weak infrastructure and weak purchasing power, an industry conference heard.

"Some companies are now moving out of their crisis but the overall risks involved are still high and Russia has not started its economic recovery," Claudio Teruzzi, chief of Stainless Steel International Italia s.p.a. (SSI) said on Thursday.
The region's plants are beset by economic and managerial problems while consumption growth is far from the explosive rates seen in emerging markets elsewhere, he told a Metal Bulletin conference.
Investors should not be fooled by positive economic indicators because they were often overly optimistic and overruled by the effects of financial and political instability.
Investors were put off by high inflation, volatile exchange rates, liquidity problems and unreliable banks.
The only good point were low labour costs.

Stainless steel output, which accounts for two thirds of nickel use, had collapsed in the region in 1993 and was still some 40-50 percent below early 1990s levels, and the same applied to consumption, Terruzzi said.
The region has chrome reserves, but needs to import nickel.
Terruzzi put combined output of Russia, the Ukraine, the Czech republic, Poland, Romania and Slovenia at 396,000 tonnes in 1996, up 16 percent from 1995.
Imports by the six countries plus Hungary, Albania, the Baltics, Slovakia, Bulgaria and other CIS states were put at 104,500 tonnes, up 15 percent, led by Poland and the Czech republic.
Their consumption in 1996 was 294,600 tonnes of which Russia accounted for 53 percent, Slovenia, which feeds some specialised processing units, for 17 percent, and Poland for 15 percent.
SSI and French Ugine are seeking to take a majority stake in Romanian stainless steelmaker Otelinox, where SSI has been doing hire-rolling for export for a number of years.

Austrian analyst Markus Moll of the SMR consultancy said eastern Europe was successfully exporting stainless steel bars but its imports of high-value flat products such as sheet and coil were due to rise.
